It maps past behavioral patterns into probabilistic predictions of full-week inactivity across four horizons. The model assumes stationarity and causal sufficiency of the input features. Temporal leakage arises from random splitting without time-ordering, invalidating out-of-sample generalization. Dualities emerge between classical ML baselines (e.g., GBT) and deep architectures (e.g., Transformers), where the latter exhibit superior performance under high-dimensional, long-range dependency structures. Failure modes include overfitting to spurious correlations, incorrect temporal alignment, and lack of calibration. These issues are mitigated by enforcing temporal holdouts and conformal prediction frameworks in GSI’s Bayesian pipeline.
